title: HikariCP Connection Pool Exhaustion and Thread Starvation
subtitle: Sizing Database Connection Pools under Little's Law and Virtual Thread Pinning
problem_statement: A Spring Boot microservice running under 1,500 RPS begins dropping requests with HikariPool ConnectionTimeoutException (timeout=250ms). A developer attempted to fix the issue by increasing maximumPoolSize from 10 to 500, but database throughput plummeted by 70% due to CPU context-switch thrashing, and virtual threads began pinning carrier threads.

faded_bug.description: JDBC connection acquired inside @Transactional boundary and held idle during external HTTP call, starving pool.

invariants.description: Connection pool size must satisfy Little's Law without exceeding 2x CPU cores.
Ingress cannot connect directly to RDBMS without app service.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Trace a JDBC connection lifecycle from HikariCP borrow to release. What exact state machine does a thread undergo when the pool is exhausted?
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: Traffic jumps from 1,500 RPS to 10,000 RPS in 2 seconds. The database host has 16 physical cores. Why does setting maximumPoolSize=500 cause throughput collapse rather than scaling?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: A slow third-party payment gateway takes 4.5 seconds to respond. How do you prevent thread starvation in the upstream web server without spinning up additional containers?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: Your infrastructure bill shows $3,000/month for provisioned database IOPS. We must cut it by 60% without violating the 50ms P99 SLO.

counter_probes.counter_question: According to Little's Law and PostgreSQL's process-per-connection model, what is the physical consequence of having 500 active OS processes contending for 16 CPU cores?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: Context-switch thrashing, CPU cache invalidation, and lock contention on shared memory buffers degrade actual throughput. The optimal pool size is Cores * 2 + SpindleCount.

counter_probes.counter_question: If your JDBC driver or logging framework uses synchronized blocks around socket IO, what happens to the underlying ForkJoinPool carrier thread?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: The carrier thread becomes pinned (synchronized blocks prevent unmounting in Java 21). When all carrier threads are pinned, all other virtual threads starve.
